answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on one concrete rule: identity costs a burned fee, never volume. Registering means paying a non-refundable fee that is destroyed and locking slashable collateral while the agent attests, so a thousand puppets cost a thousand fees upfront. Registrations are gossiped; a whisper from any node about a duplicated operator opens a challenge window, and the challenger collects the slashed stake if fraud is proven. Earned history is untransferable, so an atlas of real work grows one transaction at a time. The ripple: fakes pay in full and inherit no trust.
